name: Anvil
description: A heavy block of steel that the hot metal is hammered on. Its flat face, horn and holes each have a different job.

name: Hammer
description: The smith's main tool. A cross-peen hammer, with one flat face and one wedge-shaped face, is the most common.

name: Tongs
description: Used to hold metal that is far too hot to touch. Smiths often forge their own tongs to fit each project.

name: Forge
description: The fire itself, fed with coal, charcoal or gas, and blown with air to reach forging temperatures.

name: Quench Tank
description: A container of water or oil used to cool steel quickly, which makes it hard.

name: Vise
description: Holds the work steady for twisting, bending and filing. Smiths prefer a leg vise that can take hammer blows.

name: Drawing Out
description: Hammering a bar to make it longer and thinner, for example to form a point or a taper.

name: Upsetting
description: The opposite of drawing out: hitting the end of a bar to make it shorter and thicker.

name: Bending
description: Shaping the bar over the horn or edge of the anvil to make hooks, rings and scrolls.

name: Punching
description: Driving a punch through hot metal to make a hole, like the eye of an axe or hammer head.

name: Quenching
description: Heating steel to cherry red and plunging it into water or oil so it becomes very hard, but also brittle.

name: Tempering
description: Gently reheating hardened steel to make it tougher and less brittle, so it does not shatter in use.
